messages.content: Suppose a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) converge pointwise to f(x) on [0, 1]. Does it follow that the B_n converge uniformly? Ensure that stop words constitute no more than 20% of the total words in your response.

message.content:
No. Take B_n(x) = x^n on [0,1]. Pointwise: x ∈ [0,1) gives x^n → 0; x = 1 gives x^n → 1. Define f: f(x) = 0 for x < 1; f(1) = 1. B_n → f pointwise.

Convergence is NOT uniform. Each n: sup_{x∈[0,1)} x^n = 1 (supremum as x → 1⁻). Hence ‖B_n − f‖_∞ = 1 for every n. Uniform convergence criterion fails.

The limit f is discontinuous. Uniform limits of continuous functions are continuous. Contradiction confirms non-uniformity.
